title: Noun sentence - Identifying components
description: Identify the 3 components of a noun sentence (جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة) — Mubtada, Khabar, and Muta'allaq bil khabar — in worked examples, plus the special mudhaafs that often make up the Muta'allaq bil khabar.
source: Owner's lesson notes on the noun sentence: Mubtada, Khabar, Muta'allaq bil khabar, and special mudhaafs

questions.text: What are the 3 components of a noun sentence?

options.text: Mubtada, Khabar, and Muta'allaq bil khabar
Harf of Nasb, Jaar Majroor, and Khabar
Mubtada, Khabar, and Harf of Nasb
Mubtada, Jaar Majroor, and special mudhaaf

questions.explanation: The three components of a noun sentence are Mubtada (M), Khabar (K), and Muta'allaq bil khabar (MBK).

questions.text: In the formula M(must) + is + K (optional) + MBK (optional), which component is the only one that is required?

options.text: Both Khabar and Muta'allaq bil khabar

questions.explanation: The formula marks Mubtada as "must", while Khabar and Muta'allaq bil khabar are both optional.

questions.text: When a sentence begins with a harf of Nasb, what is the Mubtada?

options.text: The first Raf'a in the sentence, regardless of the harf of Nasb
The Khabar that follows the harf of Nasb
The harf of Nasb and its ism, including chain
The harf of Nasb alone, without its ism

questions.explanation: The Mubtada is a harf of Nasb and its ism including chain, when a harf of Nasb is present.

questions.text: When there is no harf of Nasb in the sentence, what is the Mubtada?

options.text: Whatever word comes first in the sentence, status aside
The first Raf'a in the sentence, including chain

questions.explanation: Without a harf of Nasb, the Mubtada is simply the first Raf'a in the sentence, including its chain.

questions.text: How is the Khabar defined?

options.text: The first Raf'a after the Mubtada, including chain
A Jaar Majroor that follows the Mubtada
The ism of the harf of Nasb
Any Raf'a anywhere in the sentence

questions.explanation: The Khabar is the first Raf'a that comes after the Mubtada (including its chain), and it gives information about the Mubtada.

questions.text: What can function as the Muta'allaq bil khabar (MBK)?

options.text: A Jaar Majroor including chain, or a special mudhaaf
Only the harf of Nasb's ism

questions.explanation: The Muta'allaq bil khabar is additional information given as a Jaar Majroor (including chain) or a special mudhaaf.

questions.text: In "إِنَّ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ كَرِيمٌ" ("Certainly the messenger of Allah is kind"), what is the Mubtada?
questions.explanation: إِنَّ is the harf of Nasb, and رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ (the mudhaaf and mudhaaf ilayh) is its ism, so the whole chain رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ is the Mubtada.

questions.text: In the same sentence, "إِنَّ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ كَرِيمٌ", what is the Khabar?
questions.explanation: كَرِيمٌ ("kind") is the first Raf'a after the Mubtada and gives information about it, so it is the Khabar.

questions.text: In "ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ" ("Allah is the light of the skies and the earth"), what is the Mubtada, and why?

options.text: ٱللَّهُ, because there is no harf of Nasb, so the Mubtada is the first Raf'a
نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ, because it is a Jaar Majroor
ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ, because it ends the chain
ٱللَّهُ نُورُ, because it is the whole first half

questions.explanation: There is no harf of Nasb in this sentence, so the Mubtada is simply the first Raf'a, which is ٱللَّهُ.

questions.text: In the same sentence, "ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ", what is the Khabar?

options.text: There is no Khabar in this sentence

questions.explanation: نُورُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ is the first Raf'a after the Mubtada, including its whole chain, so it is the Khabar.

questions.text: In "ٱلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ" ("Peace and blessings is on you"), what is the Mubtada?

options.text: It is a harf of Nasb

questions.explanation: ٱلسَّلَامُ is the first Raf'a in the sentence, so it is the Mubtada.

questions.text: In "ٱلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ", the Khabar is left out. What role does عَلَيْكُمْ play?

options.text: It is still the Khabar, just placed differently
It is a harf of Nasb
It is the Muta'allaq bil khabar, a Jaar Majroor standing in for the missing Khabar

questions.explanation: Since Khabar is optional, عَلَيْكُمْ (a Jaar Majroor) functions here as the Muta'allaq bil khabar even though no separate Khabar is stated.

questions.text: In "إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ" ("Surely Allah is with those who have patience"), why is ٱللَّهَ the Mubtada?

options.text: Because إِنَّ is a harf of Nasb and ٱللَّهَ is its ism
Because ٱللَّهَ is a Jaar Majroor
Because ٱللَّهَ is the Khabar of مَعَ
Because ٱللَّهَ is a special mudhaaf

questions.explanation: إِنَّ is the harf of Nasb, and ٱللَّهَ is its ism, so together they form the Mubtada.

questions.text: In the same sentence, "إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ", what role does مَعَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ play, since there is no separate Khabar?

options.text: It is the Muta'allaq bil khabar
It is the ism of إِنَّ
It is a second harf of Nasb

questions.explanation: With no separate Khabar stated, مَعَ ٱلصَّابِرِينَ (built on the special mudhaaf مَعَ) functions as the Muta'allaq bil khabar, the same as عَلَيْكُمْ in ٱلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ.

questions.text: Which of these words is listed as a special mudhaaf — a word that always appears as a mudhaaf but does not necessarily mean possession or belonging?
questions.explanation: غَيْرُ ("other than/non") is one of the special mudhaafs, alongside words like كُلُّ, بَعْضُ, أَيُّ, نَفْسُ and the time/place words.

questions.text: Which special mudhaaf means "between"?
questions.explanation: بَيْنَ means "between". تَحْتَ is "under", فَوْقَ is "above", and قَبْلَ is "before".

questions.text: Which special mudhaaf means "under"?
questions.explanation: تَحْتَ means "under", the opposite of فَوْقَ ("above").

questions.text: Which special mudhaaf means "after"?
questions.explanation: بَعْدَ means "after"; قَبْلَ means "before".

questions.text: Which special mudhaaf means "has/with/at/by"?
questions.explanation: عِنْدَ is glossed as "has/with/at/by" among the special mudhaafs.

questions.text: What does غَيْرُهُ mean, as given among the special mudhaaf examples?
questions.explanation: غَيْرُهُ ("other than him") is one of the example forms shown for the special mudhaafs, alongside نَفْسِي ("myself") and مِثْلِه ("same as him").
